concepts.name: What is Biology
concepts.description: Biology as the science of life; major branches — botany, zoology, microbiology, physiology, ecology, genetics; scope and relevance of biology to medicine, agriculture and industry.

concepts.name: Characteristics of Living Organisms
concepts.description: Growth, reproduction, metabolism, cellular organisation, response to stimuli, homeostasis and evolution as the defining properties that distinguish living from non-living matter.

concepts.name: Need for Classification
concepts.description: Diversity of life and the rationale for systematic classification; identification, nomenclature and taxonomic hierarchy — kingdom to species.

concepts.name: Five Kingdom Classification
concepts.description: Whittaker's five-kingdom system — Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia; basis of classification — cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction.

concepts.name: Binomial Nomenclature
concepts.description: Linnaean binomial system; rules of nomenclature — genus and species, italicisation, author citation; ICBN/ICZN conventions.

concepts.name: Viruses, Viroids and Lichens
concepts.description: Acellular nature of viruses; structure of a typical virus — capsid, genome; viroids as naked infectious RNA; lichens as symbiotic associations of algae and fungi.

concepts.name: Microscopy and Laboratory Techniques
concepts.description: Light vs electron microscopy; magnification and resolution; staining techniques; safe handling of laboratory glassware and specimens.

concepts.name: Levels of Biological Organisation
concepts.description: Hierarchy from molecules to biosphere — cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism, population, community, ecosystem, biome, biosphere.

concepts.name: Cell Theory
concepts.description: Historical development of cell theory — Schleiden, Schwann, Virchow; the cell as the basic structural and functional unit of life.

concepts.name: Prokaryotic Cell Structure
concepts.description: Cell wall, plasma membrane, nucleoid, ribosomes, plasmids, flagella and pili in bacteria; absence of membrane-bound organelles.

concepts.name: Eukaryotic Cell Structure
concepts.description: Plant vs animal cell comparison; plasma membrane, cytoplasm, membrane-bound nucleus and organelles; compartmentalisation as an organisational principle.

concepts.name: Cell Membrane and Transport
concepts.description: Fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane; passive transport — diffusion, osmosis, facilitated diffusion; active transport and the sodium-potassium pump; endocytosis and exocytosis.

concepts.name: Nucleus and Chromosomes
concepts.description: Nuclear envelope, nucleolus, chromatin; chromosome structure — centromere, telomere, chromatids; karyotype and chromosome number.

concepts.name: Mitochondria and Energy Organelles
concepts.description: Mitochondrial structure — outer/inner membrane, cristae, matrix; mitochondria as the site of aerobic respiration; semi-autonomous nature.

concepts.name: Chloroplast Structure
concepts.description: Double membrane, thylakoids, grana, stroma; chlorophyll location; chloroplast as the site of photosynthesis; endosymbiotic origin.

concepts.name: Endomembrane System
concepts.description: Endoplasmic reticulum (smooth and rough), Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, vacuoles; protein and lipid synthesis, modification, packaging and secretion pathways.

concepts.name: Cytoskeleton and Cell Motility
concepts.description: Microfilaments, microtubules and intermediate filaments; roles in shape, intracellular transport, cell division and motility — cilia and flagella.

concepts.name: The Cell Cycle
concepts.description: Interphase (G1, S, G2) and M phase; checkpoints and cyclin-CDK regulation; significance of regulated progression for growth and genome stability; oncogene activation and tumour-suppressor loss as pathological consequences of checkpoint failure.

concepts.name: Mitosis
concepts.description: Stages — prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase; spindle apparatus; significance in growth, repair and asexual reproduction.

concepts.name: Meiosis
concepts.description: Meiosis I and II; synapsis, crossing over, independent assortment; reductional vs equational division; significance for genetic variation and gamete formation.

concepts.name: Cell Signalling
concepts.description: Signal molecules and receptors; signal transduction pathways; second messengers; paracrine, endocrine and autocrine signalling.

concepts.name: Types of Biomolecules
concepts.description: Macromolecules vs micromolecules; carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids as the four major classes; elemental composition of living matter.

concepts.name: Carbohydrates and Lipids
concepts.description: Mono-, di- and polysaccharides; structural vs storage carbohydrates; fatty acids, triglycerides, phospholipids and steroids; roles in energy storage and membranes.

concepts.name: Proteins and Protein Structure
concepts.description: Amino acids and peptide bonds; primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure; denaturation; structure-function relationship in enzymes and structural proteins; ubiquitin-proteasome degradation as the cell's mechanism for clearing misfolded proteins.

concepts.name: Enzymes and Enzyme Kinetics
concepts.description: Enzymes as biological catalysts; active site, substrate specificity, induced fit; factors affecting enzyme activity — temperature, pH, concentration; competitive and non-competitive inhibition.

concepts.name: Nucleic Acid Structure
concepts.description: Nucleotide composition — base, sugar, phosphate; DNA double helix (Watson-Crick model); RNA types — mRNA, tRNA, rRNA; base pairing rules.

concepts.name: DNA Replication
concepts.description: Semiconservative replication; helicase, DNA polymerase, primase, ligase; leading and lagging strands, Okazaki fragments; origin of replication.

concepts.name: Transcription
concepts.description: RNA polymerase and promoter recognition; initiation, elongation, termination; post-transcriptional processing — splicing, capping, polyadenylation in eukaryotes.

concepts.name: Translation and the Genetic Code
concepts.description: Codons and the genetic code — degeneracy, universality; ribosome structure and function; initiation, elongation, termination of translation; role of tRNA and aminoacyl synthetases.

concepts.name: Regulation of Gene Expression
concepts.description: Lac operon as a model of prokaryotic regulation; eukaryotic transcription factors, enhancers and silencers; epigenetic regulation — methylation, histone modification.

concepts.name: Mendelian Genetics
concepts.description: Mendel's laws of inheritance — dominance, segregation, independent assortment; monohybrid and dihybrid crosses; Punnett squares; test cross.

concepts.name: Gene Interactions and Extensions of Mendelism
concepts.description: Incomplete dominance, codominance, multiple alleles, epistasis, polygenic inheritance; deviations from simple Mendelian ratios.

concepts.name: Chromosomal Theory and Linkage
concepts.description: Chromosomal basis of inheritance; linkage and recombination frequency; gene mapping concepts; sex-linked inheritance and sex determination systems.

concepts.name: Pedigree Analysis and Human Genetic Disorders
concepts.description: Pedigree chart conventions; autosomal and sex-linked disorders — haemophilia, colour blindness, thalassemia, sickle cell anaemia; chromosomal disorders — Down, Turner, Klinefelter syndromes.

concepts.name: Mutations
concepts.description: Point mutations — substitution, insertion, deletion; frameshift vs non-frameshift effects; chromosomal mutations — duplication, deletion, inversion, translocation; mutagens.

concepts.name: Population Genetics
concepts.description: Allele and genotype frequencies; Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and its assumptions; factors disturbing equilibrium — mutation, migration, selection, drift.

concepts.name: Genetic Engineering and Recombinant DNA
concepts.description: Restriction enzymes, vectors, cloning; PCR amplification; gene cloning vs gene expression; applications in producing recombinant proteins.

concepts.name: Origin of Life
concepts.description: Theories of the origin of life — Oparin-Haldane hypothesis, Miller-Urey experiment; prebiotic chemical evolution; RNA world hypothesis.

concepts.name: Evidence for Evolution
concepts.description: Fossil record, comparative anatomy — homologous and analogous structures, embryology, biogeography and molecular evidence supporting common descent.

concepts.name: Natural Selection and Darwinism
concepts.description: Darwin's theory of natural selection; variation, heritability, differential survival and reproduction; adaptation as a product of selection; industrial melanism as a case study.

concepts.name: Modern Synthesis and Speciation
concepts.description: Integration of Mendelian genetics with Darwinian selection; mechanisms of speciation — allopatric, sympatric; reproductive isolation; adaptive radiation.

concepts.name: Human Evolution
concepts.description: Primate evolutionary trends; major hominin fossils — Australopithecus, Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Homo sapiens; bipedalism and brain size trends.

concepts.name: Human Digestive System
concepts.description: Alimentary canal organisation; digestive glands; mechanical and chemical digestion; absorption of nutrients; common digestive disorders.

concepts.name: Human Respiratory System
concepts.description: Respiratory organs and mechanism of breathing; exchange and transport of gases — O2 and CO2; regulation of respiration; respiratory disorders.

concepts.name: Human Circulatory System
concepts.description: Structure of the heart and cardiac cycle; blood composition and blood groups; double circulation; lymphatic system; ECG basics; cardiovascular disorders.

concepts.name: Excretory System and Osmoregulation
concepts.description: Structure of the nephron; mechanism of urine formation — filtration, reabsorption, secretion; osmoregulation; role of ADH and the renin-angiotensin system.

concepts.name: Nervous System and Neural Control
concepts.description: Neuron structure; resting and action potentials; synaptic transmission; central, peripheral and autonomic nervous system organisation; reflex action.

concepts.name: Endocrine System
concepts.description: Major endocrine glands and their hormones; feedback regulation of hormone secretion; hormone mechanism of action — second messengers, gene activation.

concepts.name: Locomotion and Musculoskeletal System
concepts.description: Types of muscle tissue; sliding filament theory of muscle contraction; skeletal system organisation; joints and movement; disorders of muscles and bones.

concepts.name: Immune System Overview
concepts.description: Innate vs acquired immunity; humoral and cell-mediated immunity; structure of antibodies; lymphoid organs.

concepts.name: Photosynthesis
concepts.description: Light and dark reactions; photosystems I and II; electron transport and photophosphorylation; Calvin cycle (C3 pathway); C4 and CAM adaptations.

concepts.name: Respiration in Plants
concepts.description: Glycolysis, Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain; aerobic vs anaerobic respiration; respiratory quotient; relationship between photosynthesis and respiration.

concepts.name: Plant Water Relations
concepts.description: Absorption of water by roots; transpiration and the cohesion-tension theory; ascent of sap; stomatal regulation; water potential.

concepts.name: Mineral Nutrition in Plants
concepts.description: Essential macro- and micronutrients; deficiency symptoms; nitrogen fixation — biological and industrial; nutrient uptake mechanisms.

concepts.name: Plant Growth and Hormones
concepts.description: Auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, abscisic acid and ethylene; phases of plant growth; photoperiodism and vernalisation.

concepts.name: Asexual Reproduction
concepts.description: Binary fission, budding, fragmentation, vegetative propagation; advantages and limitations compared to sexual reproduction.

concepts.name: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
concepts.description: Flower structure; microsporogenesis and megasporogenesis; pollination types; fertilisation and post-fertilisation events — endosperm and embryo development; seed and fruit formation.

concepts.name: Human Reproductive System
concepts.description: Male and female reproductive anatomy; gametogenesis — spermatogenesis and oogenesis; menstrual cycle and hormonal regulation.

concepts.name: Fertilisation and Embryonic Development
concepts.description: Fertilisation, cleavage, blastula and gastrula formation; implantation; placenta formation and function; parturition.

concepts.name: Reproductive Health and Contraception
concepts.description: Reproductive health awareness; methods of contraception; assisted reproductive technologies — IVF, ZIFT, GIFT; sexually transmitted infections.

concepts.name: Fundamentals of Animal Development
concepts.description: Stages from zygote to adult; cleavage patterns; cell fate determination — totipotency, pluripotency; significance of the embryonic axes.

concepts.name: Morphogenesis and Cell Differentiation
concepts.description: Induction and organiser regions; differential gene expression driving cell differentiation; morphogen gradients; classic experiments — Spemann organiser.

concepts.name: Stem Cells and Regeneration
concepts.description: Embryonic vs adult stem cells; pluripotency and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs); regenerative capacity across species; therapeutic applications and ethical considerations.

concepts.name: Organisms and their Environment
concepts.description: Habitat and niche; abiotic and biotic factors; adaptations to climatic extremes; concept of acclimatisation.

concepts.name: Population Ecology
concepts.description: Population attributes — density, birth/death rate, age structure; population growth curves — exponential and logistic; population interactions — competition, predation, parasitism, mutualism.

concepts.name: Ecosystem Structure and Function
concepts.description: Producers, consumers and decomposers; food chains and food webs; ecological pyramids; energy flow and the 10% law.

concepts.name: Nutrient Cycling and Succession
concepts.description: Carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus cycles; primary and secondary ecological succession; climax communities.

concepts.name: Biodiversity and Conservation
concepts.description: Levels of biodiversity — genetic, species, ecosystem; measuring biodiversity; threats — habitat loss, invasive species, climate change; conservation strategies — in-situ and ex-situ.

concepts.name: Environmental Issues and Pollution
concepts.description: Air, water and soil pollution sources and effects; ozone depletion; eutrophication; global warming and climate change; sustainable development.

concepts.name: Microbial Diversity
concepts.description: Bacteria, archaea, fungi, protozoa and viruses; methods of classification and identification; ubiquity and ecological roles of microbes; uncultured diversity (estimated >99% of species) and the microbiome as host-associated microbial communities.

concepts.name: Microbial Growth and Culture Techniques
concepts.description: Bacterial growth curve — lag, log, stationary, death phases; culture media types; aseptic technique; sterilisation methods.

concepts.name: Microbes in Human Welfare
concepts.description: Role of microbes in food production — curd, bread, fermented beverages; antibiotics and their discovery; microbes in sewage treatment and biogas production.

concepts.name: Pathogenic Microorganisms and Disease
concepts.description: Common bacterial, viral, fungal and protozoan diseases in humans; modes of transmission; Koch's postulates; principles of disease control.

concepts.name: Innate and Adaptive Immunity
concepts.description: Physical, physiological and cellular barriers of innate immunity; humoral and cell-mediated branches of adaptive immunity; primary and secondary immune response.

concepts.name: Antibody Structure and Function
concepts.description: Immunoglobulin structure — heavy and light chains, variable and constant regions; antibody classes and their functions; antigen-antibody interaction specificity.

concepts.name: Vaccination and Immunisation
concepts.description: Active vs passive immunisation; types of vaccines — live attenuated, inactivated, subunit, mRNA; herd immunity concept; immunisation schedules.

concepts.name: Immune Disorders
concepts.description: Allergies and hypersensitivity reactions; autoimmune diseases; immunodeficiency — AIDS as a case study; organ transplant rejection and immunosuppression.

concepts.name: Principles of Biotechnology
concepts.description: Genetic engineering and bioprocess technology as the two core techniques; tools — restriction enzymes, vectors, host cells; basic bioreactor design.

concepts.name: Biotechnology Process Applications
concepts.description: Recombinant insulin and vaccine production; transgenic plants and Bt crops; gene therapy concepts; molecular diagnostics — ELISA, PCR-based detection.

concepts.name: Genomics and Proteomics
concepts.description: Genome sequencing strategies; the Human Genome Project; functional vs structural genomics; proteomics and the study of the complete protein complement of a cell.

concepts.name: CRISPR and Genome Editing
concepts.description: CRISPR-Cas9 mechanism — guide RNA, Cas9 nuclease, double-strand break repair; applications in gene knockout and correction; ethical and biosafety considerations.

concepts.name: Introduction to Bioinformatics
concepts.description: Biological databases — GenBank, UniProt, PDB; sequence file formats; the role of computation in modern biology.

concepts.name: Sequence Alignment
concepts.description: Pairwise alignment — global (Needleman-Wunsch) and local (Smith-Waterman); scoring matrices; multiple sequence alignment; BLAST search strategy.

concepts.name: Computational Phylogenetics
concepts.description: Distance-based and character-based tree-building methods; molecular clock hypothesis; interpreting phylogenetic trees from sequence data.

concepts.name: Structural Bioinformatics
concepts.description: Protein structure prediction approaches — homology modelling, ab initio methods; structural databases; relationship between sequence, structure and function.

concepts.name: Introduction to Systems Biology
concepts.description: Holistic vs reductionist approaches to biology; the concept of biological networks — gene regulatory, metabolic, signalling networks.

concepts.name: Gene Regulatory Networks
concepts.description: Network motifs — feedback and feedforward loops; modelling approaches for transcriptional regulation; emergent properties such as bistability and oscillation.

concepts.name: Metabolic Network Modelling
concepts.description: Flux balance analysis; stoichiometric modelling of metabolic pathways; constraint-based reconstruction of genome-scale metabolic networks.

concepts.name: Synthetic Biology
concepts.description: Engineering biological circuits from standardised parts; design-build-test cycle; applications in biosensing and biomanufacturing; biosafety considerations.

concepts.name: Three Domain System
concepts.description: Woese's three-domain classification from 16S rRNA phylogeny; distinguishing features of Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya; Archaea-Eukarya phylogenetic proximity; molecular evidence for the three-domain tree of life.

concepts.name: Endosymbiotic Theory
concepts.description: Origin of mitochondria and chloroplasts from free-living bacteria; evidence: double membranes, 70S ribosomes, circular DNA, binary fission; primary and secondary endosymbiosis; genome reduction over evolutionary time; implications for the diversity and complexity of eukaryotic life.

concepts.name: Eukaryotic Supergroups and Protist Diversity
concepts.description: Major eukaryotic supergroups (SAR, Excavata, Amoebozoa, Archaeplastida); ecological significance of protists; endosymbiotic plastid origins in algal lineages; protists as ecological drivers and model organisms for cell biology.

concepts.name: Fungal Biology
concepts.description: Chitin cell walls; absorptive heterotrophy; hyphal growth and mycelium organisation; major fungal groups (Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, Zygomycetes, Chytridiomycetes); sexual and asexual reproduction; decomposer, pathogenic and mycorrhizal roles in ecosystems.

concepts.name: Plant Diversity and Alternation of Generations
concepts.description: Sporophyte and gametophyte alternation as the universal plant life cycle; trends across bryophytes, lycophytes, ferns, gymnosperms and angiosperms; structural adaptations to terrestrial life; progressive gametophyte reduction as a macro-evolutionary trend in land plants.

concepts.name: Cladistics and Phylogenetic Thinking
concepts.description: Synapomorphies as defining shared derived characters; monophyletic, paraphyletic and polyphyletic groups; parsimony and maximum likelihood as inference principles; reading phylogenetic trees (branch lengths, node support, outgroups); tree thinking as core quantitative literacy for all of biology.

concepts.name: Viral Replication and Lifecycle
concepts.description: Lytic and lysogenic cycles in bacteriophage; Baltimore classification of viruses by genome type (seven classes); attachment, entry, replication, assembly and release; retroviruses and reverse transcriptase; RNA-dependent RNA polymerase in RNA viruses.

concepts.name: Horizontal Gene Transfer
concepts.description: Transformation, transduction and conjugation as natural HGT mechanisms; HGT as the primary driver of prokaryotic genome evolution; antibiotic resistance spread as an applied consequence; the prokaryotic phylogeny as a reticulate network rather than a tree; evidence for ancient HGT events in eukaryotes.

concepts.name: Apoptosis and Programmed Cell Death
concepts.description: Intrinsic pathway (cytochrome c release, Bcl-2 family, apoptosome formation, caspase cascade); extrinsic pathway (death receptors, FADD, initiator caspases); executioner caspase activation and hallmark morphological changes; physiological roles in embryonic development, immune selection and homeostatic tissue turnover.

concepts.name: Epigenetics and Chromatin Regulation
concepts.description: DNA methylation and CpG island silencing; histone code hypothesis (acetylation, methylation, phosphorylation); chromatin remodelling complexes; heterochromatin versus euchromatin domains; genomic imprinting; X-chromosome inactivation (Barr body); evidence for transgenerational epigenetic inheritance.

concepts.name: Non-coding RNA Biology
concepts.description: siRNA and RISC-mediated RNA interference; miRNA biogenesis (Drosha, Dicer) and post-transcriptional repression; lncRNA roles in chromatin regulation and transcriptional control; piRNA and transposon silencing in the germline; ribozymes as catalytic RNA molecules.

concepts.name: Core Signal Transduction Pathways
concepts.description: MAPK/ERK cascade (RTK to Ras to Raf to MEK to ERK); Wnt/beta-catenin pathway (frizzled, Dishevelled, beta-catenin stabilisation, TCF/LEF transcription); Notch signalling (membrane-bound ligand, gamma-secretase cleavage, NICD nuclear translocation); JAK-STAT pathway; cross-pathway interactions and mechanisms of signalling specificity.

concepts.name: DNA Damage Response and Repair
concepts.description: Damage types (oxidative lesions, UV-induced pyrimidine dimers, single- and double-strand breaks); Base Excision Repair (glycosylase, AP endonuclease); Nucleotide Excision Repair (recognition, dual incision, gap-fill); Mismatch Repair (strand discrimination, nick-directed excision); Homologous Recombination versus NHEJ for DSBs; ATM/ATR checkpoint kinase activation.

concepts.name: Bioenergetics and Thermodynamics of Life
concepts.description: Gibbs free energy (delta G) and spontaneity; exergonic versus endergonic reactions and metabolic directionality; ATP as the universal energy currency; coupled reactions and energetic rationale; NAD+/NADH and FAD/FADH2 as electron carriers; chemiosmotic principle as the unifying theme of energy transduction.

concepts.name: Transposable Elements and Genome Organisation
concepts.description: DNA transposons (cut-and-paste via transposase); retrotransposons (copy-and-paste via RNA intermediate); LINEs, SINEs and LTR retrotransposons; transposable elements as approximately 50% of the human genome; the C-value paradox; genome organisation (coding, non-coding, repetitive elements, gene families, pseudogenes).

concepts.name: Molecular Evolution and Neutral Theory
concepts.description: Kimura's neutral theory and nearly-neutral theory; synonymous versus nonsynonymous substitutions; dN/dS ratio as a statistical test for natural selection; molecular clock hypothesis and its limitations; selective sweeps and their genomic signatures; purifying selection versus positive selection at the sequence level.

concepts.name: Evolutionary Developmental Biology
concepts.description: Hox genes as master regulators of body plan axis specification; genetic toolkit (conserved regulatory genes: Pax6, Distal-less, Tinman); deep homology across phyla; modularity and developmental constraints; heterochrony and heterotopy as mechanisms generating morphological variation across evolutionary time.

concepts.name: Community Ecology
concepts.description: Competitive exclusion principle (Gause's law) and coexistence mechanisms; character displacement and niche partitioning; keystone species and trophic cascades; intermediate disturbance hypothesis; succession (facilitation, tolerance, inhibition models); island biogeography theory; species diversity indices (Shannon, Simpson).

concepts.name: MHC and Antigen Presentation
concepts.description: MHC class I (all nucleated cells, endogenous peptides, CD8+ cytotoxic T cell activation); MHC class II (APCs, exogenous peptides, CD4+ helper T cell activation); antigen processing pathways (proteasome, TAP, lysosomal); peptide-MHC complex and TCR recognition geometry; self-tolerance via thymic positive and negative selection; MHC restriction; allograft rejection mechanism.

concepts.name: Animal Cognition
concepts.description: Problem-solving and tool use as evidence of flexible, non-instinctive behaviour; comparative cognition methodology across species; the contested evidence for theory of mind in non-human animals and the methodological challenges of inferring mental states from behaviour.

concepts.name: Animal Communication
concepts.description: Signal modalities — visual, auditory and chemical (pheromone) communication; honest-signalling theory and the handicap principle explaining why costly signals can remain reliable; the role of communication in territorial, social and mating contexts.

concepts.name: Foraging Behaviour
concepts.description: Optimal foraging theory as a cost-benefit framework predicting diet and patch-use decisions; the marginal value theorem for patch-leaving decisions; risk-sensitive foraging when energy state affects the optimal strategy.

concepts.name: Human Behavioural Ecology and Evolutionary Psychology
concepts.description: Applying behavioural-ecology principles (kin selection, reciprocal altruism, parental investment) to human behaviour; proposed human behavioural universals and the evidence and controversy surrounding them; cultural evolution as a second, faster inheritance system operating alongside genetic evolution.

concepts.name: Innate Behaviour and Instinct
concepts.description: Fixed action patterns as stereotyped, largely unmodifiable behavioural sequences; sign stimuli as the triggers that release them; reflexes distinguished from more complex instinctive behaviour; the genetic basis of innate behaviour as a heritable trait shaped by natural selection.

concepts.name: Kin Selection and Altruism
concepts.description: Hamilton's rule (rB > C) as the quantitative condition for altruism to be favoured by selection; inclusive fitness as fitness measured through both direct reproduction and the reproductive success of relatives; reciprocal altruism as an alternative route to cooperation between non-relatives.

concepts.name: Learning and Behaviour
concepts.description: Habituation as the simplest form of learning; classical and operant conditioning as associative learning mechanisms; imprinting as a time-limited form of learning during a critical period; observational (social) learning as a route to acquiring behaviour without direct trial and error.

concepts.name: Mating Systems and Sexual Selection
concepts.description: Mate choice as a distinct selective force from survival-based natural selection; intrasexual selection (competition between same-sex individuals) versus intersexual selection (mate preference); mating system diversity — monogamy, polygyny, polyandry; sexual dimorphism as an evolutionary outcome of sexual selection.

concepts.name: Social Behaviour and Eusociality
concepts.description: Costs and benefits of group living — resource competition and predation risk versus cooperative defence and information sharing; dominance hierarchies as a mechanism for resolving repeated resource conflicts; eusociality in social insects — reproductive division of labour, overlapping generations, cooperative brood care.

concepts.name: Comparative Genomics
concepts.description: Synteny — conserved gene order across related genomes — as evidence of shared ancestry; distinguishing orthologs (same gene, different species) from paralogs (duplicated genes within a genome); the pan-genome concept for characterising genomic diversity within a species.

concepts.name: Genome Sequencing Technologies
concepts.description: Sanger sequencing principle contrasted with next-generation sequencing platforms (short-read and long-read); genome assembly strategies — de novo assembly versus reference-guided mapping; sequencing depth and coverage as determinants of assembly quality.

concepts.name: Multi-Omics and Statistical Genomics
concepts.description: Transcriptomics (RNA-seq), proteomics and metabolomics as complementary layers of biological information; integrating multiple omics data types to build a systems-level picture; the multiple-testing problem in high-throughput biology and why raw p-values from thousands of simultaneous tests are statistically misleading without correction.

concepts.name: Agricultural and Forensic Biotechnology
concepts.description: Marker-assisted selective breeding as a non-transgenic application of molecular genetics to crop improvement; DNA fingerprinting principles (short tandem repeat profiling) applied to forensic identification and paternity testing; chain-of-custody and statistical interpretation of DNA evidence.

concepts.name: Bioprocess Engineering
concepts.description: Bioreactor design parameters — aeration, agitation, temperature and pH control; fermentation scale-up from laboratory to industrial volume; downstream processing steps (cell separation, purification, formulation) for recovering a biological product from culture.

concepts.name: Gene Therapy
concepts.description: Viral versus non-viral gene-delivery vectors and their trade-offs in efficiency and safety; ex vivo versus in vivo gene therapy strategies; clinical trial history including early setbacks (SCID trials, adenoviral toxicity) and recent approved therapies as evidence-based case studies.

concepts.name: Anaerobic Respiration and Fermentation
concepts.description: ATP generation when oxygen is limiting or absent; lactic acid fermentation in animal muscle and lactic acid bacteria; alcoholic fermentation in yeast; comparative ATP yield of aerobic versus anaerobic pathways; physiological (oxygen debt) and industrial (brewing, dairy) contexts.

concepts.name: Hallmarks of Cancer
concepts.description: The Hanahan-Weinberg hallmarks of cancer as an integrative framework: sustained proliferative signalling, evasion of growth suppressors, resistance to apoptosis, replicative immortality, angiogenesis induction, invasion and metastasis, and metabolic reprogramming — each hallmark traced back to a specific breakdown in normally regulated cell behaviour.

concepts.name: Cell Adhesion and Tissue Organisation
concepts.description: Cadherins, selectins and integrins as families of cell-adhesion molecules with distinct binding logic; epithelial-mesenchymal transition as a reversible loss of adhesion and polarity; how adhesion loss underlies both normal development (gastrulation, wound healing) and pathological invasion.

concepts.name: Cell Junctions and the Extracellular Matrix
concepts.description: Tight junctions, desmosomes and gap junctions as sealing, anchoring and communicating structures between cells; extracellular matrix composition — collagen, proteoglycans, fibronectin and integrin receptors; the matrix as a structural and signalling scaffold for tissue architecture.

concepts.name: Cytoskeletal Motility
concepts.description: Actin-myosin-based cell crawling distinct from muscle contraction; microtubule motor proteins (kinesin, dynein) driving intracellular cargo transport; the 9+2 axoneme structure and ciliary/flagellar beating; cytoskeletal remodelling during division, migration and shape change.

concepts.name: Energetics of Membrane Transport
concepts.description: Passive versus active transport distinguished by free-energy cost along an electrochemical gradient; primary active transport (ATP-driven pumps) versus secondary active transport (symport and antiport using an existing gradient); quantitative reasoning about transport direction from concentration and charge.

concepts.name: Biology of Ageing and Senescence
concepts.description: Cellular senescence as an irreversible proliferative arrest distinct from apoptosis; telomere shortening as a replicative clock; the hallmarks-of-ageing framework — genomic instability, mitochondrial dysfunction, altered intercellular communication; evolutionary theories of why ageing exists (antagonistic pleiotropy, disposable soma).

concepts.name: Organogenesis
concepts.description: Organ formation as a special case of morphogenesis driven by reciprocal induction between tissue layers; epithelial-mesenchymal interactions as a recurring organogenetic mechanism; limb-bud outgrowth and neural-tube closure as worked examples of organ-level pattern formation.

concepts.name: Regeneration Biology
concepts.description: Regenerative capacity compared across model taxa — planarian whole-body regeneration, axolotl limb regeneration, zebrafish fin and heart regeneration; blastema formation as the shared cellular mechanism; why mammalian regenerative capacity is comparatively limited.

concepts.name: Animal Body Plans and Symmetry
concepts.description: Radial versus bilateral symmetry as fundamental organisational strategies; diploblastic versus triploblastic body organisation; acoelomate, pseudocoelomate and coelomate body cavities; protostome versus deuterostome developmental patterns as a deep phylogenetic split within Bilateria.

concepts.name: Arthropod Diversity
concepts.description: The chitinous exoskeleton and moulting (ecdysis) as the defining arthropod constraint and solution; major arthropod classes — Insecta, Arachnida, Crustacea, Myriapoda; segmentation and jointed appendages as drivers of arthropods' unmatched species diversity.

concepts.name: Chordate and Vertebrate Diversity Overview
concepts.description: The four defining chordate features — notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail — and their fate in vertebrate development; an overview of the vertebrate classes (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals) as the organising framework for the four vertebrate-diversity concepts that follow.

concepts.name: Echinoderms and Deuterostome Diversity
concepts.description: Deuterostome development (blastopore becomes the anus) as the shared developmental signature linking echinoderms to chordates; Echinodermata defining features — pentaradial symmetry (secondarily derived from a bilateral ancestor), water vascular system, endoskeleton; the phylogenetic position of echinoderms as invertebrate relatives of the chordates.

concepts.name: Fish and Amphibian Diversity
concepts.description: Jawless, cartilaginous and bony fish diversity and their respective adaptations; the amphibian water-to-land transition and its anatomical prerequisites (limbs, lungs); amphibian metamorphosis as a dramatic developmental case study; amphibians' continued dependence on water for reproduction.

concepts.name: Invertebrate Diversity: Major Phyla
concepts.description: Defining features and ecological roles of the major invertebrate phyla — Porifera (sponges, cellular-grade organisation), Cnidaria (radial symmetry, nematocysts), Platyhelminthes (flatworms, acoelomate), Nematoda (pseudocoelomate roundworms), Annelida (segmented worms), Mollusca (body-plan diversity from snails to cephalopods).

concepts.name: Mammalian Diversity
concepts.description: Defining mammalian features — hair, mammary glands, endothermy, a single lower jawbone with three middle-ear bones; monotreme (egg-laying), marsupial (pouched) and placental reproductive strategies as three distinct solutions within one clade; ecological and evolutionary radiation of placental mammals.

concepts.name: Reptile and Bird Diversity
concepts.description: The amniotic egg as the key innovation freeing reptiles from an aquatic reproductive stage; reptile diversity across squamates, turtles and crocodilians; birds as a lineage nested within Reptilia (specifically within theropod dinosaurs); skeletal, respiratory and metabolic adaptations for powered flight.

concepts.name: Applied Ecology and Ecosystem Services
concepts.description: Ecosystem services classified as provisioning, regulating, supporting and cultural; economic and non-economic valuation approaches for services with no market price; environmental impact assessment as the applied framework connecting ecological science to policy decisions.

concepts.name: Advanced Biogeochemical Cycling
concepts.description: The sulfur cycle as a fourth major biogeochemical cycle alongside carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus; anthropogenic disruption of natural cycling rates — fertiliser-driven nitrogen and phosphorus loading; eutrophication mechanism in depth, from nutrient input through algal bloom to hypoxic dead zones.

concepts.name: Global Change Biology
concepts.description: Climate-driven shifts in species phenology (timing of life-cycle events) and geographic range; ocean acidification and its impact on calcifying marine organisms; biotic homogenisation as native community diversity is replaced by generalist and invasive species.

concepts.name: Landscape and Conservation Ecology
concepts.description: Habitat fragmentation and its effects on population connectivity; corridors and stepping-stone habitats as mitigation strategies; metapopulation dynamics — patch occupancy, extinction-colonisation balance; restoration ecology principles for degraded ecosystems.

concepts.name: Microbial Ecology
concepts.description: Biogeochemical roles of microbes as the principal drivers of nutrient cycling; biofilm formation and structure as a dominant microbial lifestyle; extremophiles and the habitats that select for them; soil and gut microbiome ecology as applied case studies of microbial community structure.

concepts.name: Quantitative Models of Population Growth
concepts.description: Formalises the exponential and logistic growth curves already introduced qualitatively, as differential equations — dN/dt = rN for exponential growth and dN/dt = rN(1 - N/K) for logistic growth with carrying capacity K; deriving population trajectories from these models; r-selected versus K-selected life-history strategies as ecological correlates of each growth regime.

concepts.name: Predator-Prey Population Dynamics
concepts.description: The Lotka-Volterra predator-prey equations as a coupled system of differential equations; functional response (how per-capita predation rate scales with prey density) and numerical response (how predator population responds to prey availability); boom-bust population cycles as an emergent property of the coupled system.

concepts.name: Coevolution and Species Interactions
concepts.description: Reciprocal evolutionary change between interacting species; predator-prey and host-parasite evolutionary arms races; the Red Queen hypothesis; mutualistic coevolution illustrated by pollinator specialisation; coevolution distinguished from simple parallel adaptation to a shared environment.

concepts.name: Convergent Evolution and Homoplasy
concepts.description: Convergent evolution (independent origin of similar traits) versus parallel evolution (similar traits from shared ancestral starting points); homoplasy as a source of misleading signal in phylogenetic reconstruction; classic case studies — marsupial/placental body forms, camera-eye evolution across lineages.

concepts.name: Macroevolution and Mass Extinction
concepts.description: Macroevolutionary patterns above the species level; punctuated equilibrium versus phyletic gradualism as models of tempo; background extinction rate versus the "Big Five" mass extinction events; adaptive radiation following ecological release, illustrated by post-extinction diversification.

concepts.name: Phylogeography and Historical Biogeography
concepts.description: Vicariance versus dispersal as alternative explanations for disjunct species distributions; continental drift and its imprint on present-day biogeographic patterns; molecular phylogeography — using gene-tree data to reconstruct the geographic history of populations and species.

concepts.name: The Scientific Method in Biology
concepts.description: Hypothesis formation and testing; controlled experiments — independent, dependent and control variables; sample size, replication and statistical significance; peer review and reproducibility as the foundation of biological knowledge.

concepts.name: Unifying Themes in Biology
concepts.description: Structure-function relationship as a recurring biological pattern across scales; evolution as biology's central organising theory ("nothing in biology makes sense except in the light of evolution"); homeostasis as dynamic internal balance; energy flow and matter cycling linking organisms to their environment.

concepts.name: Conservation Genetics
concepts.description: Genetic diversity as a component of population viability; inbreeding depression in small populations; effective population size versus census size; genetic rescue through managed gene flow; genetic tools for identifying management units in endangered species.

concepts.name: Genetic Testing and Counselling
concepts.description: Carrier screening for recessive disorders; prenatal diagnostic techniques — amniocentesis, chorionic villus sampling, non-invasive prenatal testing; principles of genetic counselling — risk communication, informed consent, non-directiveness; ethical considerations in predictive genetic testing.

concepts.name: Quantitative Genetics and Heritability
concepts.description: Continuous, polygenic traits contrasted with the single-locus traits of Mendelian genetics; broad-sense versus narrow-sense heritability; heritability estimation from twin and family studies; genotype-by-environment interaction and why heritability is a population-specific statistic, not a fixed property of a trait.

concepts.name: Cancer Immunology and Immunotherapy
concepts.description: Tumour immune evasion strategies as an extension of cancer's hallmark of avoiding immune destruction; immune checkpoint proteins (PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4) and how checkpoint-inhibitor drugs restore T-cell activity; CAR-T cell therapy as engineered, targeted cellular immunotherapy.

concepts.name: Cytokines and Immune Cell Signalling
concepts.description: Cytokine classes — interleukins, interferons, tumour necrosis factor — as the molecular language of immune cell communication; how cytokine signalling coordinates innate and adaptive responses; cytokine storm as pathological cytokine overproduction.

concepts.name: T-Cell Development and Immune Tolerance
concepts.description: Thymic positive and negative selection in mechanistic detail — extending the self-tolerance concept already introduced with MHC restriction; central tolerance (thymic deletion) versus peripheral tolerance (regulatory T cells, anergy); autoimmunity as a breakdown of one or more tolerance checkpoints.

concepts.name: Antimicrobial Resistance
concepts.description: Resistance mechanisms — efflux pumps, enzymatic drug inactivation (e.g. beta-lactamases), target-site modification; horizontal gene transfer as the primary route by which resistance genes spread between and across bacterial species; antibiotic stewardship as the applied response to a mechanistically understood evolutionary problem.

concepts.name: Archaea and Extremophiles
concepts.description: Archaeal distinguishing features — ether-linked membrane lipids, distinct RNA polymerase and histone-like proteins; extremophile categories — thermophiles, halophiles, acidophiles, piezophiles — and the molecular adaptations enabling survival in each extreme; biotechnological applications of extremophile enzymes (e.g. Taq polymerase).

concepts.name: The Human Microbiome
concepts.description: Gut microbiome composition and its variation across individuals and diets; microbiome-host interactions — nutrient synthesis, immune system training, gut-brain signalling; dysbiosis as a disruption of normal microbial balance linked to metabolic and inflammatory disease.

concepts.name: Diversity of Microbial Metabolism
concepts.description: Chemoautotrophy — deriving energy from inorganic chemical oxidation rather than light or organic carbon; photoautotrophy in bacteria beyond plant-style photosynthesis (purple and green sulfur bacteria); anaerobic respiration using alternative terminal electron acceptors (nitrate, sulfate, CO2); metabolic versatility as the basis of extremophile survival.

concepts.name: Alternative Splicing and RNA Diversity
concepts.description: Exon and intron definition within pre-mRNA; the spliceosome and its snRNP components; alternative splicing patterns — exon skipping, intron retention, alternative 5'/3' splice sites, mutually exclusive exons; how one gene generates multiple protein isoforms, resolving the apparent gene-count paradox of complex organisms.

concepts.name: Chromatin Structure and 3D Genome Organisation
concepts.description: Nucleosome structure (histone octamer, linker DNA) as the first level of DNA packaging; higher-order chromatin folding into 30 nm fibres and loops; topologically associating domains (TADs) and chromatin loop anchors; how three-dimensional genome architecture, distinct from the regulatory marks covered in epigenetics, constrains which genes can physically contact their enhancers.

concepts.name: Metabolic Regulation and Integration
concepts.description: Allosteric regulation and feedback inhibition as control points in metabolic pathways; hormonal control of glycolysis, gluconeogenesis and glycogen metabolism; metabolic integration across fed versus fasted physiological states; rate-limiting enzymes as points of pharmacological and physiological intervention.

concepts.name: Protein Quality Control and Autophagy
concepts.description: Molecular chaperones (heat-shock proteins) assisting correct protein folding; the unfolded protein response to endoplasmic-reticulum stress; macroautophagy, microautophagy and chaperone-mediated autophagy as degradation routes distinct from the ubiquitin-proteasome system; proteostasis collapse in neurodegenerative disease.

concepts.name: Audition and the Vestibular System
concepts.description: Ear anatomy — outer, middle and inner ear; hair-cell mechanotransduction in the cochlea; tonotopic coding of sound frequency along the basilar membrane; the vestibular system's role in balance and detection of head movement.

concepts.name: Autonomic and Stress Physiology
concepts.description: The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis as the body's principal stress-response pathway; sympathetic versus parasympathetic balance in acute stress; cortisol's wide-ranging physiological effects; allostatic load as the cumulative cost of chronic stress-response activation.

concepts.name: Regional Organisation of the Brain
concepts.description: Forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain divisions; cerebral cortex lobes and their principal functional localisation; the limbic system and its role in emotion and memory; cerebellar and brainstem contributions to movement coordination and vital autonomic functions.

concepts.name: Cognitive Neuroscience and Consciousness
concepts.description: Attention and executive function as top-down cognitive control mechanisms; the search for neural correlates of consciousness; split-brain studies as evidence for hemispheric specialisation and the limits of unified conscious experience.

concepts.name: The Neurobiology of Learning and Memory
concepts.description: Synaptic plasticity — long-term potentiation and depression — as the cellular substrate of learning; Hebbian learning ("cells that fire together, wire together"); the hippocampus's role in declarative memory formation, contrasted with procedural memory systems elsewhere in the brain.

concepts.name: Neural Circuits and Computation
concepts.description: Excitatory and inhibitory circuit motifs (feedforward inhibition, lateral inhibition) as building blocks of neural computation; rate coding versus temporal coding as alternative strategies for representing information; central pattern generators as an example of circuit-level rhythmic behaviour.

concepts.name: Neurodegenerative Disease
concepts.description: Alzheimer's disease pathology — amyloid-beta plaques and tau neurofibrillary tangles; Parkinson's disease and the selective loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra; protein misfolding and aggregation as a shared mechanistic theme across neurodegenerative disorders.

concepts.name: Neurodevelopment
concepts.description: Neurulation as the embryonic formation of the neural tube; neuronal migration guided by radial glia; synaptogenesis and activity-dependent synaptic pruning; critical periods as windows of heightened neural plasticity.

concepts.name: Neurotransmitter Systems
concepts.description: Major neurotransmitters — glutamate and GABA as the principal excitatory/inhibitory pair, dopamine, serotonin, acetylcholine, norepinephrine; ionotropic versus metabotropic receptor mechanisms; synaptic vesicle release and neurotransmitter clearance by reuptake or enzymatic degradation, extending the synaptic transmission already introduced.

concepts.name: Sensory Transduction
concepts.description: The general principle of sensory transduction — converting a physical or chemical stimulus into a graded receptor potential; major receptor categories (photoreceptors, mechanoreceptors, chemoreceptors, thermoreceptors); sensory adaptation and the coding of stimulus intensity by action-potential frequency.

concepts.name: Sleep and Circadian Biology
concepts.description: REM and NREM sleep stages and their distinct physiological signatures; the suprachiasmatic nucleus as the master circadian pacemaker; molecular clock genes (CLOCK, BMAL1, PER, CRY) generating a roughly 24-hour transcriptional-translational feedback loop.

concepts.name: The Visual System
concepts.description: Eye anatomy — cornea, lens, retina; the phototransduction cascade in rod and cone photoreceptors; retinal processing by bipolar and ganglion cells; the visual pathway from retina through the optic nerve to the visual cortex.

concepts.name: Blood Physiology and Haemostasis
concepts.description: Blood cell types and haematopoiesis from bone-marrow stem cells; the haemostasis sequence — vascular spasm, platelet plug formation, coagulation cascade; ABO and Rh blood group genetics and transfusion compatibility.

concepts.name: Comparative Animal Physiology
concepts.description: Gas-exchange strategies across animal groups — gills, tracheal systems, book lungs, alveolar lungs — and the surface-area-to-volume constraints each solves; open versus closed circulatory systems; osmoregulatory strategies compared across marine, freshwater and terrestrial habitats.

concepts.name: Endocrine Disorders and Feedback Pathology
concepts.description: Hyper- and hypo-secretion disorders as failures at different points in an endocrine feedback loop; negative feedback (most hormone axes) contrasted with the positive feedback of oxytocin during childbirth; hormone-receptor mutations as a distinct disease mechanism from abnormal hormone level.

concepts.name: Exercise Physiology
concepts.description: Cardiovascular and respiratory adaptations to acute and chronic exercise; aerobic versus anaerobic training effects on muscle fibre composition and mitochondrial density; VO2 max as an integrative measure of oxygen-delivery and oxygen-use capacity.

concepts.name: Homeostasis and Thermoregulation
concepts.description: Negative feedback as the general principle underlying homeostatic control loops, illustrated by thermoregulation — vasodilation and vasoconstriction, sweating, shivering and behavioural responses to a hypothalamic set point; osmoregulation (already detailed mechanistically in the excretory system) framed here as a second worked example of the same feedback logic.

concepts.name: The Integumentary System
concepts.description: Skin structure — epidermis, dermis and hypodermis; functions of skin beyond covering — protection, thermoregulation, sensation, vitamin D synthesis; the wound-healing sequence (haemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, remodelling).

concepts.name: The Lymphatic System
concepts.description: Lymphatic vessel structure and one-way lymph flow; lymph node architecture and its role in filtering pathogens and antigen presentation; lymphedema as a consequence of impaired drainage; the lymphatic system's dual role in fluid balance and immune surveillance.

concepts.name: Muscle Physiology and Energetics
concepts.description: Motor units and the size principle of recruitment; slow-twitch (oxidative) versus fast-twitch (glycolytic) muscle fibre types; ATP sources for contraction across timescales — creatine phosphate, anaerobic glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation; mechanisms of muscle fatigue.

concepts.name: Mycorrhizae and Root Symbioses
concepts.description: Arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal associations as widespread plant-fungal mutualisms extending root absorptive surface; the rhizobium-legume symbiosis mechanism in detail — nodule formation, nitrogenase and oxygen exclusion by leghaemoglobin; symbiotic nutrient exchange as a case study in mutualistic coevolution.

concepts.name: Phytochrome and the Molecular Basis of Photoperiodic Flowering
concepts.description: Building on the qualitative introduction to photoperiodism, this concept develops the molecular mechanism: phytochrome interconversion between Pr and Pfr forms in response to red/far-red light; the critical-night-length model of flowering induction; florigen (FT protein) as the mobile signal transmitted from leaf to shoot apex; circadian gating of the photoperiodic response.

concepts.name: Plant Biotechnology Applications
concepts.description: Plant tissue culture and micropropagation exploiting totipotency; Agrobacterium-mediated transformation as the principal plant genetic engineering method; transgenic crop traits beyond pest resistance — herbicide tolerance, biofortification (e.g. Golden Rice); marker-assisted breeding as a non-transgenic alternative.

concepts.name: Plant Defence Mechanisms
concepts.description: Structural defences (thorns, trichomes, thickened cuticle) versus chemical defences (alkaloids, terpenoids, phenolics as secondary metabolites); constitutive versus induced defence responses; plant-herbivore and plant-pathogen interactions as an evolutionary arms race distinct from, but connected to, animal immune defence.

concepts.name: Plant Stress Physiology
concepts.description: Drought stress responses — stomatal closure, osmotic adjustment; salinity stress and ion toxicity; reactive oxygen species generation under stress and the antioxidant defence system; abscisic acid (ABA) as the central stress-signalling hormone linking multiple stress pathways.

concepts.name: Plant Tissue Systems
concepts.description: Meristematic tissue (apical and lateral) versus permanent tissue; the three permanent tissue systems — dermal, ground and vascular; xylem and phloem structure and their distinct transport roles, providing the structural foundation that underlies water transport and photosynthate distribution.

concepts.name: Secondary Growth and Plant Anatomy
concepts.description: Vascular cambium and cork cambium as lateral meristems responsible for growth in girth; wood (secondary xylem) and bark (secondary phloem plus periderm) formation; annual growth rings as a record of seasonal cambial activity.

concepts.name: Seed Germination and Dormancy
concepts.description: Seed structure — seed coat, embryo, endosperm/cotyledon food reserves; physiological and physical dormancy mechanisms and their adaptive significance; environmental germination triggers — water, temperature, light; hypogeal versus epigeal germination patterns.

concepts.name: Comparative Animal Reproductive Strategies
concepts.description: Oviparity, viviparity and ovoviviparity compared across animal groups; parental investment theory and its prediction of trade-offs between offspring number and care; r-selected versus K-selected reproductive strategies as ends of a life-history continuum.

concepts.name: Hormonal Regulation of Reproduction
concepts.description: The hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis; pulsatile GnRH secretion and its translation into the menstrual cycle's hormonal pattern; mechanisms of hormonal contraception (feedback suppression of the HPG axis); principles of hormone replacement in reproductive medicine.

concepts.name: Evolutionary Systems Biology
concepts.description: How gene-regulatory and metabolic networks themselves evolve, not just the genes within them; robustness and evolvability as related but distinct network properties; a systems-level perspective on why some network architectures are more evolutionarily accessible than others.

concepts.name: Quantitative Modelling of Biological Systems
concepts.description: Ordinary-differential-equation models of gene and protein concentration dynamics as a quantitative extension of the network-motif descriptions already introduced; parameter estimation from experimental time-course data; sensitivity analysis for identifying which parameters most strongly determine model behaviour.
